notes.subject: car
notes.text: Mostly Generation 4 pickup coverage, usually blurred, but often a snorkel shows. Only one other country has a snorkel on Gen 4.

notes.subject: line
notes.text: Outer edge lines are always solid white; centre lines are yellow, solid or dashed.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Concrete or wooden utility poles with an L-shaped crossbar.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: A grey SUV is often seen following the Street View car.

notes.subject: plate
notes.text: Long white front plates; the rear plate is square and yellow.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: A mobile network brand called Safaricom appears in almost every city and exists only here.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Direction signs are green with white border and text, often showing road numbers in white or yellow.

notes.subject: sign
notes.text: Other road signs are mostly red and white, though not very frequent.

notes.subject: pole
notes.text: Pole markings often carry a skull and a danger warning.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Repurposed vans with colourful wraps are everywhere; the wrap design differs from the ones next door.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Many eucalyptus trees with long clumped leaves and smooth bark, though they also occur elsewhere.

notes.subject: car
notes.text: Generation 3 coverage often shows a roof rack and a snorkel; some has no visible car.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Signs reading PO BOX followed by two numbers give a postcode; the three digits after the hyphen narrow down the region.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The far west around the big lake is the most farmed part: farms, grassy hills and tall eucalyptus.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The area around Kitui is semi-arid and often hilly, with light orange sandy soil.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: Coconut palms mark the coast, rarely also parts of Taita-Taveta.

notes.subject: other
notes.text: Endless stick fences are common around Narok.

notes.subject: architecture
notes.text: Pale bricks with thick mortar form walls along the coast; mud-and-stick houses occur in the west and on the coast.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: North of the big volcano on the southern border, it can be seen to the south, often hidden in cloud.

notes.subject: landscape
notes.text: The B9 in the northeast is fully unpaved with bright reddish-orange dirt and many roadside trees, mostly flat.
